AiConnectIn.description:
POST /settings/ai/connect: the key as it was pasted. The provider is read from the
key's own form and from nothing else.
AiConnectIn.title: AiConnectIn

AiLink.description: A provider connected with a pasted key. The key itself is never in any answer.
AiLink.title: AiLink

BodyProblem.description:
A body the screen built wrongly (a missing key, a wrong JSON type, an unknown key).
Never something the engineer typed: those come back as a `Refusal` with words.
BodyProblem.title: BodyProblem

BodyProblemItem.description: One place where a body does not fit, as FastAPI says it: where and why.
BodyProblemItem.title: BodyProblemItem

BriefEvent.description: `brief`: a Brief in this tender's chat started or changed state.
BriefEvent.title: BriefEvent

BriefStarted.description:
Work was started for the Lead: the new Brief's id. Its reply arrives on the chat
stream, and a `brief` event says when its state changes.
BriefStarted.title: BriefStarted

CardQuestion.description: One question in `payload.questions` of a `question` card.
CardQuestion.title: CardQuestion

ChoiceSetting.description: A setting that takes one of a few values.
ChoiceSetting.title: ChoiceSetting

DecideIn.description:
POST /projects/{project_id}/findings/{finding_id}/decide: which of the two options the
engineer takes.
DecideIn.title: DecideIn

Finding.description:
A conflict or risk a member found in the tender, with where it was read. Once the
Lead raises it, it is a decision: the Lead's opinion and two options for the engineer.
Finding.title: Finding

FindingEvent.description:
`finding`: a Finding was recorded, queued, raised or settled, or its note changed.
The screen replaces it by id, or adds it at the end.
FindingEvent.title: FindingEvent

FindingPart.description: data-finding (id: the Finding's id): the Lead raised this Finding here.
FindingPart.title: FindingPart

Findings.description: GET /projects/{project_id}/findings: every Finding of the tender.
Findings.title: Findings

Home.description:
GET /home: everything the frame and the Home place show. It never refuses: what
cannot be read is said inside the answer.
Home.title: Home

HomeSummary.description: The Lead's words about the tenders it may speak of, and when it wrote them.
HomeSummary.title: HomeSummary

LeadBlock.description:
Why the Lead cannot start work now. For every tender: no AI is connected; the provider
refused the key when ONE last listed its models; the AI consent is not given; the day's or
the month's Spending Cap is reached; Engineer Records cannot be opened. For one tender: it is
a Confidential Project, `ai.confidential_on_device` is on and no model on this computer is
connected. No network is not known before work starts: it shows as `offline`.
LeadBlock.title: LeadBlock

Lesson.description: One Lesson Learned the Lead keeps about the engineer, in Engineer Records.
Lesson.title: Lesson

Lessons.description: GET /engineer/lessons: every Lesson Learned that was not removed.
Lessons.title: Lessons

LessonsEvent.description: `lessons`: a lesson was saved, changed, removed or put back.
LessonsEvent.title: LessonsEvent

Member.description:
A team member's identity card and record: the Lead QS, the Checking QS or a
specialist. Every list carries the whole member, so no route gives one alone.
Member.title: Member

MemberEvent.description: `member`: a member joined or became permanent, or its `state` or `doing` changed.
MemberEvent.title: MemberEvent

MemberModel.description: The AI model a member works with now.
MemberModel.title: MemberModel

MemberRecord.description: Counted from the member's real work in ONE; zeros for a new member.
MemberRecord.title: MemberRecord

MemberTool.description: A tool a member may use, with the label the screen shows for it.
MemberTool.title: MemberTool

Members.description: GET /team/members: the team that stays from tender to tender, for Settings.
Members.title: Members

MoneySetting.description: A setting that is an amount of money, as exact decimal text.
MoneySetting.title: MoneySetting

NumberSetting.description: A setting that is a number within limits, as exact decimal text.
NumberSetting.title: NumberSetting

PlanApproveIn.description: POST /projects/{project_id}/plan/approve: approves the plan and its team as shown.
PlanApproveIn.title: PlanApproveIn

PlanChange.description:
A Suggested change to an approved plan: the plan as it would be. It is accepted or
rejected with POST /projects/{project_id}/plan/change. `stages[*].status`, `result` and
output ids are always the current plan's.
PlanChange.title: PlanChange

PlanChangeIn.description:
POST /projects/{project_id}/plan/change: accepts or rejects the Suggested change that
is on screen.
PlanChangeIn.title: PlanChangeIn

PlanEvent.description:
`plan`: the plan was proposed, approved or changed, a stage moved, or a Suggested
change came or went. The screen replaces its plan and reloads the members.
PlanEvent.title: PlanEvent

PlanPart.description: data-plan (id: the plan's id): the Lead proposed this version, or a change to it, here.
PlanPart.title: PlanPart

PlanView.description: The one body the plan travels in: the GET, the three POSTs and the `plan` event.
PlanView.title: PlanView

Profile.description:
GET and PUT /engineer/profile: what the engineer told ONE about themselves, as stored
in Engineer Records.
Profile.title: Profile

ProfileIn.description:
PUT /engineer/profile: the seven fields as they stand. A half-filled profile is saved.
The handler checks each value and refuses with words (PROFILE_BAD_VALUE): a name longer
than 80 characters, a position or company longer than 120, a currency that is not three
capitals. The bounds here only stop a runaway body.
ProfileIn.title: ProfileIn

Refusal.description: Every refused request of a contract route. `error` is always a pair, never a string.
Refusal.title: Refusal

RoomEvent.description: `room`: a message was written in the team room, or its `raised` changed.
RoomEvent.title: RoomEvent

RoomMessage.description:
One message in a tender's team room. It also travels as the `data-room` part of the
reply it was written in.
RoomMessage.title: RoomMessage

RoomMessageIn.description: POST /projects/{project_id}/room: what the engineer writes to the team.
RoomMessageIn.title: RoomMessageIn

RoomPage.description: GET /projects/{project_id}/room: one page of the team room.
RoomPage.title: RoomPage

RoomRaise.description:
What a raised message became in the engineer's conversation: a Finding (`id` is the
Finding's) or a card (`id` is the card's). It is the id of that part and of its waiting item.
RoomRaise.title: RoomRaise

SettingChoice.description: One value a choice setting can take, with its label.
SettingChoice.title: SettingChoice

SettingEvent.description: `setting`: a setting changed, by the screen or by the Lead.
SettingEvent.title: SettingEvent

SettingIn.description:
PATCH /settings/{key}. A toggle takes true or false; every other control takes text
(a choice's value, or an exact decimal). To put a setting back, send its `recommended`.
SettingIn.title: SettingIn

Settings.description:
GET /settings: every setting the screens draw from data. The profile, the AI links,
the Connectors, the Backup and the team have their own routes.
Settings.title: Settings

SetupEvent.description: `setup`: a part's state or bytes changed.
SetupEvent.title: SetupEvent

SetupPart.description: One part ONE needs beyond the installer, and how far its download is.
SetupPart.title: SetupPart

SetupState.description: GET /setup/parts, POST /setup/parts/retry and the `setup` event: the Automatic setup.
SetupState.title: SetupState

SetupStepStates.description: Each first-launch step: how it was passed, or null when it was not yet.
SetupStepStates.title: SetupStepStates

SetupSteps.description: The answer GET /setup and PUT /setup/{step} already give, typed for the new gate.
SetupSteps.title: SetupSteps

Source.description:
Where a fact comes from: the source the Sheet, the view and the source card already read
(`Source` in ui/src/deliverables/types.ts). `kind` is the ledger's own word and the list is
open: an agent's word for a place in a file ("boq", "quote"), "file" for a tender fact, or
ONE's "calculation", "engineer", "chat", "web", "prices", "sample". Only "sample" has a rule
(the sample pill); a kind the screen does not know is drawn as a plain titled source.
Source.title: Source

SourcesPart.description:
data-sources (id: the Brief's id): what the reply rests on, as far as the core can prove:
the sources of its figures, then the places the Lead read in this work.
SourcesPart.title: SourcesPart

Stage.description:
One stage of a tender plan: who owns it, its days, what it hands over and what the
engineer signs off at its end.
Stage.title: Stage

StageApproveIn.description:
POST /projects/{project_id}/plan/stages/{stage_id}/approve: signs off a stage of the
plan as shown. A sign-off cannot be undone.
StageApproveIn.title: StageApproveIn

StageOutput.description:
Something a stage hands over: a Deliverable, a file, the Project Map or the tender
summary.
StageOutput.title: StageOutput

StagePart.description: data-stage (id: the stage's id): this reply ends the stage and asks for its sign-off.
StagePart.title: StagePart

SteerPart.description: data-steer (id: a new id): what the engineer wrote while this work ran.
SteerPart.title: SteerPart

StoredMessageMark.description: The keys this contract adds to `metadata` of a message in GET /chat/{chat_id}/messages.
StoredMessageMark.title: StoredMessageMark

TeamMember.description: A member as one tender sees it.
TeamMember.title: TeamMember

TeamMembers.description: GET /projects/{project_id}/members: the team of one tender.
TeamMembers.title: TeamMembers

TenderEvent.description: `tender`: the tender's row, or what waits in it, changed. Replaces both.
TenderEvent.title: TenderEvent

TenderPlan.description:
A tender's plan: the stages dated back from the submission date, the team, and the
estimate the engineer approves with it.
TenderPlan.title: TenderPlan

TenderRow.description:
One tender in a line: the row Home lists and the header its own place draws.
The core remembers it for a closed project, so reading it opens nothing.
TenderRow.title: TenderRow

TenderView.description:
GET /projects/{project_id}/tender, and the `tender` event: a tender's header and what
waits for the engineer in it.
TenderView.title: TenderView

Text.description:
ONE's own words, or a short name an agent wrote for the screen, in both languages.
Neither side is ever empty: where nothing is known the pair itself is `null`.
Text.title: Text

ToggleSetting.description: A setting that is on or off.
ToggleSetting.title: ToggleSetting

Undoable.description: A removal that can be taken back with POST /undo/{undo} for `window_ms`.
Undoable.title: Undoable

UnreadPart.description: One part of a file ONE could not read (added to a file's JSON as `unread`).
UnreadPart.title: UnreadPart

UnreadableTender.description: A project whose Project Records cannot be opened: nothing else about it is known.
UnreadableTender.title: UnreadableTender

WaitingItem.description:
One thing the engineer must answer, and the id of the part that shows it in that
conversation. By kind, `id` is: "plan" and "plan_change" the plan's id (its last `data-plan`
part); "stage" the stage's id (`data-stage`); "decision" the Finding's id (`data-finding`);
"unfinished" the Brief's id (its reply is "<id>-reply"); any card kind the card's id
(`data-card`).
WaitingItem.title: WaitingItem

info.title: QS Mind ONE: the Phase 1 contract
